title: Embed + Rerank API compatibility reconciliation: pagination, status mapping, and contract
creator: Maria Chen
description: Reconcile subtle behavioral differences between the legacy embeddings+rerank endpoints and the new unified endpoint surface. Goal is to publish a stable compatibility layer that preserves client expectations for pagination tokens, error status and error body shapes, and deterministic ordering semantics while enabling the runtime to route to optimized rerank pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Backward-compatible pagination semantics: existing cursor tokens accepted by the new endpoint for the common cases (offset-based and tokenized cursors).
New cursor tokens are opaque but include versioning so clients can detect unsupported formats and trigger migration guidance.

HTTP status mapping: every error type emitted by the runtime must map to one of the documented HTTP status codes and a stable error_code string (eg 'rate_limit_exceeded', 'model_unavailable', 'bad_request.pagination').
Error body contract: top-level fields 'error_code' (string), 'message' (string), and optional 'retry_after' (integer seconds) for 429s. No nested objects under 'error' key for compatibility.
Deterministic rerank ordering: tie-breaker behavior documented (stable by input id then score then timestamp) and validated by tests to match legacy behavior for identical input sets.
A feature flag and compatibility-mode header exist so customers can opt into strict legacy behavior or the new optimized path during rollout.
Migration docs, examples, and a compatibility test harness published to Developer Docs and included in the SDKs before GA.
No regression in existing customers' production traffic during canary >= 95% of requests over 72 hours; SLOs for error-rate and latency preserved.
implementation_notes: Introduce an input adapter layer that translates legacy query parameters (page, per_page, cursor) to unified request shapes. Adapter should preserve behavior for ambiguous cases (eg page=0 treated as page=1).

Cursor format: adopt a base64-encoded JSON payload with a 'v' field for version and an 'o' field for offset when possible; legacy opaque tokens must be consumed by a backward parser that maps into v1 representation.
Error mapping table implemented at gateway layer; runtime errors annotated with canonical error_code strings before HTTP conversion. Gateway must avoid adding extra nesting to error responses.
Routing policy: compatibility-mode header 'X-Redwood-Compat: legacy' forces the adapter and legacy sorter; default behavior uses optimized rerank pipeline with documented tie-breakers.
Add server-side tests that replay production request samples to verify identical output ordering and pagination boundaries under compatibility-mode.
SDK changes: add helpers for encoding/decoding new cursor format and for translating legacy tokens; publish minor version updates with migration notes.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy adapter + error mapping behind feature flag; expose compatibility header; route 1% of traffic for customers with highest embeddings usage.
Phase 2 (Expanded Rollout): Increase to 10% after 7 days of stability, publish migration guidance and SDK helpers; run automated comparison jobs for a sample corpus.
Phase 3 (Opt-out Sunset): After 6 weeks of stable metrics and customer feedback, begin nudging customers to non-legacy path and schedule opt-out deprecation with 90-day notice.
Provide a rollback plan: remove adapter and revert header behavior if error-rate or customer complaints cross threshold defined in SLO runbook.
qa_plan: Unit tests for cursor encode/decode for both legacy tokens and new tokens, including malformed tokens and edge offsets.
Integration tests that assert HTTP status mapping for a matrix of simulated runtime errors (model OOM, unavailable, quota, invalid args).
Golden tests: deterministic rerank outputs for canonical test sets compared against legacy service outputs in compatibility-mode.
Load test verifying pagination stability and no increased tail latency for paged queries at 95th/99th percentiles.
metrics: compat_mode_error_rate: errors/hour when X-Redwood-Compat header is present
migration_token_success_rate: percent of legacy tokens successfully parsed
pagination_mismatch_rate: percent of paged responses where item sets differ vs legacy for identical inputs
latency_p95/99: ensure p99 latency not regressed beyond +15% when compatibility adapter is active
